title: Linear Search
description: Scan nums from left to right and return the index of the first value equal to target, or -1 if it never appears.

title: Largest Element
description: Return the largest value in a non-empty array in a single pass.

title: Second Largest Element
description: Return the largest value that is strictly smaller than the maximum, or -1 if no such value exists. Do it in one pass by tracking the best and second-best values.

title: Longest Run of Ones
description: nums contains only 0s and 1s. Return the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s.
referenceCode:
def max_consecutive_ones(nums):
    best = 0
    run = 0
    for value in nums:
        run = run + 1 if value == 1 else 0
        best = max(best, run)
    return best

title: Move Zeros to the End
description: Move every 0 in nums to the end while keeping the other values in their original order. Do it in place with a write pointer, then return nums.

title: Find the Missing Number
description: nums holds n distinct values taken from 0, 1, ..., n, so exactly one value in that range is missing. Return it using O(1) extra space.

examples.explanation: Every value up to n = 2 is present except 2.

title: Majority Element
description: One value in nums appears more than n / 2 times. Return it. Moore's voting algorithm finds it in one pass with a single candidate and a counter.

sourceTitle: Print the matrix in spiral manner
title: Spiral Order
description: Return the values of an m × n matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting from the top-left corner and moving right.

title: Pascal's Triangle: One Value
description: Rows and columns of Pascal's triangle are numbered from 1. Return the value at row r, column c. It equals the binomial coefficient C(r - 1, c - 1), which you can build with a running product.

title: Pascal's Triangle: One Row
description: Return row n of Pascal's triangle (rows numbered from 1).
referenceCode:
def pascal_row(n):
    row = [1]
    value = 1
    for i in range(1, n):
        value = value * (n - i) // i
        row.append(value)
    return row

title: Pascal's Triangle: First N Rows
description: Return the first n rows of Pascal's triangle. Each value is the sum of the two values above it.

title: Rotate a Matrix
description: Rotate an n × n matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place, then return it. Transposing the matrix and then reversing every row does exactly that.

title: Three Sum
description: Return every distinct triplet [a, b, c] from nums with a + b + c = 0. Write each triplet in ascending order; the triplets themselves may come in any order, but none may repeat.

title: Four Sum
description: Return every distinct quadruplet [a, b, c, d] from nums whose sum equals target. Write each quadruplet in ascending order; the list may be in any order, without repeats.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
description: Return the largest sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray. Kadane's algorithm keeps the best sum ending at the current index and drops it as soon as it turns negative.

title: Next Permutation
description: Rearrange nums into the next permutation in lexicographic order, in place, and return it. If nums is already the largest arrangement, wrap around to the smallest (ascending) one.

title: Elements Above n / 3
description: Return every value that appears more than n / 3 times in nums, in ascending order. There can be at most two such values, so an extended voting algorithm needs only two candidates.

sourceTitle: Find the repeating and missing number
title: Repeating and Missing Number
description: nums has n values from 1 to n, except one value appears twice and one is missing. Return [repeating, missing]. The sums of values and of squares give two equations for the two unknowns.
referenceCode:
def find_repeating_missing(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    sum_diff = sum(nums) - n * (n + 1) // 2
    square_diff = sum(value * value for value in nums) - n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) // 6
    both = square_diff // sum_diff
    repeating = (sum_diff + both) // 2
    return [repeating, repeating - sum_diff]

title: Count Inversions
description: An inversion is a pair of indices i < j with nums[i] > nums[j]. Return how many there are. Count them while merge sorting: each time a right-half value is placed first, it jumps every remaining left-half value.

title: Reverse Pairs
description: Count pairs of indices i < j with nums[i] > 2 × nums[j]. A merge sort can count them between the two sorted halves before merging.
